title: Calibration Budgets and Preprocessing Sensitivity in Cycloidal Transmission Error Models
content: Calibration of cycloidal reducer transmission error models requires measurements across load, speed and temperature. This study quantified the accuracy cost of reducing the calibration set from 224 to 96 measurements using the public DaRUS-4454 dataset. Linear complex ordinary least squares (OLS) and quadratic ridge regression were evaluated on the same angular grid. Complete operating levels were held out, and D-optimal, A-optimal and maximin selection were compared with 30 seeded random designs. Reduced ridge tuning used only the selected responses. Across 19 retrospective validation conditions, D-selected OLS used 57.1% fewer calibration responses and yielded a mean waveform root mean square error of 19.456 µrad versus 19.319 µrad for full OLS. The paired increase was 0.137 µrad (0.71%; descriptive 95% interval: −0.039 to 0.305 µrad). The paired comparison reused identical operating conditions. The study also audited all 243 measurement records. In a separate speed holdout analysis, a nominal 90% empirical error envelope for full ridge covered 56 of 56 cases at each of the three lower speeds and 0 of 56 at the highest speed. For this reducer, calibration reduction had a small observed average error cost on the retrospective cohort, while the coverage test revealed sensitivity to speed extrapolation.
